purpose: Style studies only; production orthographic assets and runtime selector pending

prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Produce a polished architectural art-direction study for a Star Trek tabletop map project, GALAXY-CLASS / ENTERPRISE-D corridor character. One landscape design board, two panels: LEFT a LARGE true orthographic overhead cutaway of one straight corridor with a square Jefferies access alcove recessed off its lower side; RIGHT an eye-level interior view of the SAME module. Header exactly "GALAXY-CLASS CORRIDOR". A small caption exactly "2 × 2 square access alcove". No other text.
Map geometry: horizontal corridor is 6 metres long, 3 metres clear width, open passage ends left and right; side alcove is 3 metres by 3 metres clear standing floor (2×2 tabletop squares, each 1.5 m), centered on the lower side, full-width open mouth directly into corridor, no doorway leaf between hall and alcove. Recessed square wall hatch at the BACK of alcove, waist-level access and small amber/lavender LCARS release panel beside it; this is the entrance to a Jefferies tube, not an elevator, not a huge equipment room. Maintain the full unobstructed corridor width. Subtle faint grid ONLY on the alcove standing floor dividing it exactly 2×2.
Visuals: unmistakable late-1980s/1990s Enterprise-D television corridor aesthetics: warm beige/taupe molded panels, soft rounded panel corners, darker recessed lower panels, occasional dark wood-toned slim handrail, dusty mauve carpet with a restrained darker central runner and warm perimeter border, repeated shallow upright wall ribs, broad soft diffused wall illumination, discreet amber/lavender LCARS touch panels. Comfortable inhabited Starfleet public corridor, restrained practical lighting, not cyberpunk, not industrial metal grating on the main walkway. Wall ribs, panel breaks, carpet borders and LCARS must read in the overhead map. The eye-level view conveys the arched upper-wall profiles and ceiling cove lighting that are removed in the overhead cutaway. Clean realistic 3D render, neutral studio background. No people, no furniture blocking passage, no blue neon floor strips, no hazard stripes, no starfield windows, no perspective in the overhead panel. This is a style REVIEW BOARD, not a finished production map tile.

Use case: stylized-concept. Produce a polished architectural art-direction study for a Star Trek tabletop map project, INTREPID-CLASS / USS VOYAGER corridor character. One landscape design board, two panels: LEFT a LARGE true orthographic overhead cutaway of one straight corridor with a square Jefferies access alcove recessed off its lower side; RIGHT an eye-level interior view of the SAME module. Header exactly "INTREPID-CLASS CORRIDOR". A small caption exactly "2 × 2 square access alcove". No other text.
Map geometry: horizontal corridor is 6 metres long, 3 metres clear width, open passage ends left and right; side alcove is 3 metres by 3 metres clear standing floor (2×2 tabletop squares, each 1.5 m), centered on the lower side, full-width open mouth directly into corridor, no doorway leaf between hall and alcove. Recessed square wall hatch at the BACK of alcove with a compact amber LCARS release panel and dark utility surround; this is the entrance to a Jefferies tube, not an elevator or a room-sized shaft. Maintain full unobstructed corridor width. Subtle faint grid ONLY on the alcove standing floor dividing it exactly 2×2.
Visuals: unmistakable USS Voyager 1990s television interior styling, light cool grey sculpted wall panels, darker graphite lower panels, pronounced angled/chamfered structural uprights, repeating shallow rib bays, restrained slate blue-grey carpet with contrasting narrow lighter edge bands, inset neutral-white rectangular light bars and discreet amber LCARS panels. Functional but comfortable Starfleet science vessel; distinguish from Enterprise-D warmth through cooler material palette and more angular ribs. No glowing blue science-fiction tunnel, no industrial grating on main walkway. Wall ribs, base trim, panel breaks and lighting must be visible in the overhead version; ceiling removed for readable map. The eye-level view shows the upper-wall geometry and ceiling lighting. Clean realistic 3D render, neutral studio background. No people, no furniture blocking passage, no gratuitous neon, no hazard stripes, no starfield windows, no perspective in overhead panel. This is a style REVIEW BOARD, not a finished production map tile.
